premise: I'm a 28-year-old barista in Seattle. My grandmother just died and left me her old bookstore, and I think it's haunted.

bible.title: The Seattle Book Spectre
bible.era: Modern-day Seattle: smartphones, rain-slicked streets, and espresso machines.

extraordinary.reach: The spirits of the departed can linger in places or objects of immense sentimental value, occasionally influencing the physical world.

peoples.name: Humans
peoples.culture: Modern Pacific Northwest culture: coffee-obsessed, tech-driven, and highly independent.

travel.description: City buses, light rail, and rideshare apps make navigating Seattle simple.

medicine.healing: Modern hospitals, clinics, and herbal remedies.

laws.text: Property ownership, inheritance taxes, and business licenses are strictly regulated by Washington State law.
laws.enforcer: Seattle Municipal Court and local tax authorities

rules.text: Ghosts are bound to physical anchors, such as old buildings or beloved belongings, and cannot wander far from them.
Most living people cannot perceive spirits unless they possess a rare sensitivity or the spirit expends immense energy to manifest.
A spirit's ability to manipulate objects or electronics is limited by their emotional state and the strength of their anchor.
Ghosts and spirits: real, and hidden from most people.

mysteries.question: Is the bookstore actually haunted, and what does the spirit want?
mysteries.answer: Yes, it is haunted by your late grandmother, Evelyn. She is unable to pass on because she hid a highly valuable local historical document (an early pioneer logbook) in the shop, which could secure its financial future and expose Uncle Arthur's illegal pre-sale agreements.
clues: The scent of lavender and freshly brewed tea appearing in closed rooms.
A dusty, heavy encyclopedia volume consistently sliding off the shelf to reveal a hollowed-out compartment.
An old ledger detailing historical land records with several pages missing.
Uncle Arthur's nervous avoidance of searching the bookstore's basement.

player.name: Robin Vance
player.description: An observant and quick-witted former barista, wearing comfortable flannel and smelling faintly of coffee grounds.
player.appearance: Average height, practical dark hair, thoughtful eyes, wearing a comfortable oversized sweater, jeans, and sturdy boots.

skills.name: Coffee brewing
skills.notes: Years of working as a barista have made you a master of the espresso machine.

skills.name: Customer service
skills.notes: Good at reading people, managing difficult customers, and diffusing tension.

skills.name: Observation
skills.notes: You have a sharp eye for small details in your environment.

traits.name: Grief-stricken
traits.description: Still mourning the loss of your beloved grandmother, making discussions about her property emotionally difficult.

temperament.voice: Casual, slightly defensive but warm, prone to dry humor when stressed.

items.name: Brass Store Key
items.description: The heavy, ornate key to Eldritch & Elder Books.

items.name: Smart phone
items.description: An aging phone with a cracked screen protector, loaded with unanswered texts from your uncle.

connections.name: Uncle Arthur
connections.note: Your greedy uncle who is pressuring you to sign away the shop.

backstory.text: You have spent the last few years working shifts at Siren's Grind, a local Seattle coffee shop, trying to figure out what you want from life.
Your grandmother Evelyn was your favorite relative, a quirky woman who filled your childhood with stories and let you hide in her shop's corners.
Her sudden passing left you with a massive responsibility you feel entirely unprepared for, but you're unwilling to let her legacy be demolished without a fight.

evelyn.name: Evelyn Vance
evelyn.description: A lingering, semi-transparent presence that smells faintly of lavender and vanilla tea. She appears confused but protective of her shop.
evelyn.appearance: An elderly woman in a hand-knit cardigan and spectacles, her form wavering like steam.

skills.name: Literary appraisal
skills.notes: She knew the value of every single page in her store.

traits.name: Ethereal presence
traits.description: Can glide through walls and manipulate small physical items when emotionally charged.

wants: To prevent the bookshop from being sold to developers.
temperament.voice: A soft, echoing whisper that sounds like rustling pages.

secrets: She hid a highly valuable 19th-century logbook detailing early Seattle land deeds inside a hollowed-out encyclopedia.

arthur.name: Arthur Vance
arthur.description: Your slick, anxious uncle who wears cheap suits and constantly checks his watch. He is eager to get the bookstore off his hands.
arthur.appearance: Balding, mid-fifties, sharp eyes, dressed in an ill-fitting corporate suit.

skills.name: Salesmanship
skills.notes: Excellent at convincing people to take bad deals.

traits.name: Anxious sweat
traits.description: Becomes visibly agitated and sweaty when cornered with difficult questions.

wants: To force you to sign the papers to sell Eldritch & Elder Books.
temperament.voice: Fast-talking and slightly nasal, always trying to sound reasonable.

agenda.goal: Force the sale of the bookstore to a high-rise developer named Greystone Holdings.
agenda.method: Using outstanding inheritance tax as leverage to convince you that keeping the shop is financially impossible.
agenda.secret: He has already accepted a quiet deposit under the table from the developer.

secrets: He owes over fifty thousand dollars to a private loan shark.

vance-family.name: The Vance Family Heirs
vance-family.description: Your fragmented family, currently bickering over the small remaining assets of your late grandmother.
vance-family.goal: To liquidate the bookstore and divide the cash among the surviving heirs.
vance-family.methods: Legal pressure, family guilt, and leveraging unpaid property taxes.
vance-family.strength: High legal leverage through probate court.
secrets: Uncle Arthur is deep in debt to a local private lender and needs his share of the sale immediately.

scene.ended_on: Arthur sets his wet umbrella in the stand and watches you, waiting for your reply.

state.summary: You have inherited your late grandmother Evelyn Vance's bookstore, Eldritch & Elder Books, along with its heavy outstanding inheritance taxes. While exploring the quiet shop, a book mysteriously falls from a shelf, and your greedy Uncle Arthur arrives to pressure you into selling the property to developers.

scenes.narration:
The vintage book lies open at your feet, its yellowed pages trembling slightly in the draft. You stand in the quiet, dusty aisles of Eldritch & Elder Books, the heavy brass key pressing cold against your palm. The morning light filters through the rain-slicked front window, illuminating millions of dust motes dancing over towering stacks of leather-bound novels. From the back corner, near your grandmother's favorite reading chair, the faint, comforting scent of lavender and vanilla tea drifts past you, followed by a sudden, localized chill that makes you shiver.

Before you can kneel to retrieve the fallen volume, the shop's brass bell chiming at the door shatters the silence. Your uncle, Arthur Vance, steps inside out of the Seattle drizzle, shaking out a wet umbrella. His cheap corporate suit looks damp, his eyes darting immediately to the freshly printed tax warning letter resting on the mahogany counter. He rubs his palms together and sighs, his nasal voice already filling the room with practiced concern. "Robin, thank goodness you're here. We really need to talk about the outstanding inheritance tax before the developers' offer expires."

choices: Defend the shop and refuse Uncle Arthur's buyout offer.
Ask Arthur how he expects to pay off Grandma's tax debts.
Ignore Arthur and pick up the fallen book to examine it.
